title: HUD Integration Notes
summary: How the HUD connects to the game world. Visual rules, interaction patterns, data mapping. For Bobby 2.
content:
HUD Integration Notes

Steffen | 2026-03-16 For Bobby 2. This is how the HUD and game become one thing.

The Core Principle

The HUD is NOT a UI overlay stapled onto the game. It's a COMMAND CENTER overlaid on the game world. The cool blue frosted glass panel CONTRASTS with the warm office rooms above, creating visual depth: warm world above, cool control layer below. The temperature contrast is the signature.

When a player looks at the full screen (game + HUD), they should see a WARM LIVING WORLD with a COOL CONTROL LAYER. Two temperatures on one screen = sophistication + clarity. The blue glass says "you are in control."

PATRIK DIRECTIVE (2026-03-16): Blue, not warm amber. Fresh game energy. Contrasts with warm office. References: Trello thickness, Vegas oversized text, "old people can read em young people love em."

Visual Connection Points

1. Temperature Contrast (replaces Material Continuity)

The HUD's blue frosted glass (#0B1628) CONTRASTS with the warm wood/amber visible in the game rooms. This is intentional. Warm above, cool below. The contrast creates visual depth and makes the HUD feel like a command layer, not furniture.

2. Light Bleeds (warm-to-cool transition)

Where the HUD's curved top edge meets the game view, warm light from the office rooms above bleeds DOWN onto the blue glass. This creates a beautiful warm-to-cool gradient transition at the boundary. CSS gradient overlay: a thin strip of warm amber (#FFB74D at 8-10% opacity) fading into the blue glass across the top 6-8px.

Bobby implementation: absolute-position a ::before pseudo-element on the HUD container. linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(255, 183, 77, 0.08), transparent), height 8px, full width. The warm-to-cool blend is the magic.

3. The Sims Curved Silhouette

This is THE signature shape. Kept from the warm design. A gentle convex arch along the top edge of the HUD. Center is highest, sides taper down. Now rendered in blue frosted glass instead of walnut. The curve catches light differently on glass: sharper highlight on the edge, transparency fade at the apex.

The curve serves three purposes:

  • Recognition. You see this shape and know it's a game HUD, not a web toolbar.
  • Personality. Flat rectangles are boring. The curve has character.
  • Information architecture. The center height bump draws your eye to the project section.

Bobby implementation: Use clip-path or an SVG mask on the HUD container. The background image (hud-blue/hud-strip-bg.png) has the shape baked in. Overlap the game view by the curve's height so the game shows through the transparent areas.

4. Color Temperature Adaptation

The blue glass HUD adapts subtly to the game's time of day:

  • Warm night mode (default): Deep navy glass, cyan glow accents. Maximum warm/cool contrast.
  • Daylight mode: Slightly lighter/brighter blue glass (sky reflection). Harmonizes with blue sky above.
  • Celebration mode: Blue glass with confetti particles and gold sparkle accents.

Bobby implementation: CSS custom properties. --hud-panel-base, --hud-accent, --hud-highlight, --hud-glow. See Blue Palette Quick Reference below.

Data Mapping: What the HUD Shows

The HUD surfaces REAL state. Not mock data, not placeholder text. Here's what maps to what.

Agent Row (left 30%)

HUD Element Data Source Update Frequency
Agent portrait catalog/characters/state/{name}-idle.png (cropped to face) Static
Status ring color Agent status from current-priorities.md or API Every 30s
Agent name Hardcoded per agent Static
Active highlight (1.2x size) Currently selected agent On click

Status ring colors:

  • Green (#4CAF50, glow): ACTIVE (agent is running, producing output)
  • Amber (#FFB74D, pulse): BUSY (agent is processing, waiting on dependency)
  • Red (#EF5350, pulse): BLOCKED (agent cannot proceed, needs intervention)
  • Gray (#9E9E9E, no glow): IDLE / DONE (agent has no current task)

Agent order (left to right): Bobby, Elon, Cleo, Mom, Steffen, Alex, Steve, Jacob, Colton, Elmo, Tony. Show 7-8 at a time. Horizontally scrollable if needed. Active/blocked agents sort to the front.

Project Section (middle 45%)

HUD Element Data Source
Project name Section headers from current-priorities.md
Progress bar fill Task completion ratio (done/total in that project section)
Task count "N/M" Count of completed vs total tasks
Pill state Derived: any blocked task = blocked pill, all done = complete pill
Recent task text Last updated item text from the project section

Projects to show (pulled from current-priorities.md):

  • AI ADVISORY (the product build)
  • AMBITION (client site + social)
  • CORNER BUILD (this game/dashboard itself)
  • ISA VIDEO (brand video deadline)
  • KOHRS (social retainer)
  • OUTREACH (email campaign)

Show 3-4 pills at a time. Scroll/paginate for more. Sort by: blocked first, then active by recency, then completed.

Chat Input (right 25%)

HUD Element Data Source
Selected agent portrait Same as Agent Row, linked to selection
Agent name in placeholder Dynamic: "Message {agent}..."
Last message preview Last line from relay-inbox.jsonl for that agent context
Send action Write to relay-outbox.jsonl (Bobby 3 handles the wire)

Stats Bar (top edge)

Stat Calculation
Active count Agents with green ring
Busy count Agents with amber ring
Blocked count Agents with red ring
Done count Agents with gray ring

The "blocked" count should always be visually distinct (slightly brighter, bold) because blocked = action needed.

Two HUD States

Expanded (Default)

  • Full strip visible: agent row + project section + chat input + stats bar
  • 15-20% of screen height
  • All information scannable at a glance
  • See: hud-target-v1.png and hud-target-v2.png

Collapsed (Zen Mode)

  • Thin strip: just status dots + minimal chat input + stats count
  • 6-8% of screen height
  • Maximum game view
  • Expand button (chevron) in center of curved top edge
  • See: hud-target-v3.png

Toggle between states: click the expand/collapse button, or keyboard shortcut (Tab or Escape).

Transition animation: the HUD slides down/up with a slight bounce (ease-out spring). 300ms. The game view resizes to fill. CSS transition: height 300ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1).

Interaction Patterns

Click Agent Portrait

  • Selects that agent (ring gets highlight glow, 1.2x scale)
  • Chat input switches to that agent's context
  • Project section highlights projects that agent is working on
  • In the game view above, that agent's room gets a subtle pulse/highlight

Click Project Pill

  • Expands slightly to show 2-3 subtasks below
  • The agent portraits involved in that project get a brief pulse
  • In the game, the rooms of agents working on that project get subtle highlights

Hover Project Pill

  • Shows a one-line tooltip with the most recent update text
  • The progress bar animates a subtle shine sweep (left to right, 1s)

Click Blocked Indicator

  • Immediately opens chat with the blocked agent
  • Shows the blocker reason as the last message preview
  • Prioritizes resolving the block

Send Chat Message

  • Text input -> send button or Enter
  • Message writes to relay-outbox
  • Chat preview updates with "Sent: {message}" in dimmed text
  • The agent portrait does a brief acknowledgment animation (subtle nod)

Responsive Behavior

Desktop (1440px+)

Full HUD as designed. All three sections visible.

Tablet (768-1440px)

  • Project section shows 2 pills instead of 3-4
  • Agent portraits are slightly smaller (48px instead of 64px)
  • Chat input gets its own row below (stacks vertically)

Mobile (< 768px)

  • HUD becomes a bottom navigation bar
  • Agent row becomes a horizontal scroll of tiny portrait dots
  • Project section is hidden (swipe up to reveal)
  • Chat input is a floating action button that opens a fullscreen chat overlay

Agent Portraits (Crossy Road, multi-size)

Full set at projects/steffen/catalog/characters/crossy-road/:

  • 13 agents x 3 sizes (24px, 48px, 128px) = 39 character PNGs
  • {agent}-48.png for HUD circle frames (head + shoulders + primary prop)
  • {agent}-24.png for pills/status indicators (head silhouette + color)
  • {agent}-128.png for game room detail view (full character + all props)
  • See projects/steffen/avatar-decisions.md for full asset map

DEPRECATED (warm amber, kept for reference only)

Old warm assets at projects/steffen/catalog/hud/ and warm targets at visual-target/hud/hud-target-v*.png are DEPRECATED. Bobby 2 uses BLUE only.

  • scripts/generate-hud-blue-targets.py -- Blue HUD full-screen targets (NEW)
  • scripts/generate-hud-blue-assets.py -- Blue HUD individual components (NEW)
  • scripts/generate-crossy-characters.py -- All 13 agents, 3 sizes each (NEW)
  • scripts/generate-hud-targets.py -- DEPRECATED warm targets
  • scripts/generate-hud-assets.py -- DEPRECATED warm components
  • scripts/generate-hud-portraits.py -- DEPRECATED warm portraits
  • scripts/generate-hud-extras.py -- DEPRECATED warm extras

Blue Palette Quick Reference (for Bobby 2)

Role Hex CSS Variable
Panel base #0B1628 --hud-panel-base
Electric blue (accent) #2196F3 --hud-accent
Ice blue (highlight) #64B5F6 --hud-highlight
Cyan glow #4FC3F7 --hud-glow
Text primary #F5F5F5 --hud-text
Text secondary #90CAF9 --hud-text-dim
Glass effect rgba(13, 71, 161, 0.15) --hud-glass
Panel border rgba(100, 181, 246, 0.2) --hud-border

The 5-Second Test

If someone glances at the HUD for 5 seconds, they must be able to answer:

  1. How many agents are active right now? (stats bar)
  2. Which project needs attention? (blocked pill, red ring)
  3. What's the most advanced project? (progress bar fill comparison)
  4. Who should I talk to? (agent portraits with status)

If ANY of those takes longer than 5 seconds to answer, the HUD fails. Clarity over cleverness. Information density is the product's advantage, but it has to be SCANNABLE, not overwhelming.

The HUD is the bridge between "fun game" and "real work tool." Both sides must be present in every pixel.
